newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Prices not sole factor in rate cut - Bank/Portugal.
newsitem.headline: Prices not sole factor in rate cut - Bank/Portugal.

text.p: Inflation was important but it was not the only factor considered when the Bank of Portugal opted to cut key rates on Monday, Bank governor Antonio de Sousa told Reuters.
"Inflation is not the decisive factor and you can see that from looking at some of the decisions (on rates) that we have taken in the past months," he said.
"We look at a series of indicators and obviously inflation is an important indicator. The objective of the central bank is price stability but with exchange rate stability," he said.
"The two factors have always got to be present. Also the evolution of interest rates at the European level, in the first place, and then at world level (is important)," de Sousa added.

The Bank cut its draining rate, the rate at which it absorbs excessive liquidity, by 40 basis points to 6.40 percent, and shaved 10 basis points off its repurchase rate to 6.90 percent, both effective Tuesday.
De Sousa spoke briefly after a luncheon for European Monetary Institute (EMI) chairman Alexandre Lamfalussy who is in Portugal for celebrations marking the Bank of Portugal's 150th anniversary.

De Sousa refused to comment on whether the Bank of Portugal had more room to ease rates. "Every week, we analyse the situation and if this analysis points to this (a cut) it will be made, if not, no," the governor said.
"There has been good domestic news, ranging from inflation to the approval of the (1997) budget (by parliament)," de Sousa added.
